item.title: In final State of the State, Evers pushes for school funding, end to gerrymandering
item.description: In his eighth and final State of the State address Tuesday night, Gov. Tony Evers on Tuesday night said Republicans have chronically underfunded Wisconsin schools and blamed them for increased property taxes after negotiations for a tax cut stalled this week. The post In final State of the State, Evers pushes for school funding, end to gerrymandering appeared first on WPR.

item.title: Wisconsin high school student addresses lack of ‘critical’ funding support for youth entrepreneurships
item.description: Junior high school student, Sophia Knetter, discusses the common misconceptions about starting a youth-run business, noting the advantages of being young. The post Wisconsin high school student addresses lack of ‘critical’ funding support for youth entrepreneurships appeared first on WPR.

item.title: Farm bankruptcies tick up in Wisconsin, US
item.description: Bankruptcy filings were 46 percent higher than in 2024, according to an American Farm Bureau Federation report, with more than a third of filings in the Midwest. The post Farm bankruptcies tick up in Wisconsin, US appeared first on WPR.

item.title: She Slangs Wood on a mission to empower, educate Milwaukee
item.description: She Slangs Wood's Tonda Thompson is on a mission to educate and empower people in Milwaukee through woodworking. The post She Slangs Wood on a mission to empower, educate Milwaukee appeared first on WPR.

item.title: 3 northeast Wisconsin towns call for 1-year moratorium on data centers
item.description: The towns of Two Creeks, Two Rivers and Mishicot all approved resolutions calling on Manitowoc County to place a one-year moratorium on new data center projects. The post 3 northeast Wisconsin towns call for 1-year moratorium on data centers appeared first on WPR.

item.title: Public health, green groups sue EPA over repeal of rule supporting climate protections
item.description: A coalition of health and environmental groups sued the Environmental Protection Agency on Wednesday, challenging the rescinding of a scientific finding that has been the central basis for U.S. action to regulate greenhouse gas emissions and fight climate change. The post Public health, green groups sue EPA over repeal of rule supporting climate protections appeared first on WPR.

item.title: Here today, gone tomorrow: Open water where visitors thronged Apostle Islands ice caves days ago
item.description: On Monday, visitors walked across the frozen surface of Lake Superior to see the ice caves at the Apostle Island National Lakeshore. By Wednesday morning, any chance of getting another glimpse at that fairytale seemed to be over. At least for this winter. The post Here today, gone tomorrow: Open water where visitors thronged Apostle Islands ice caves days ago appeared first on WPR.

item.title: Senate passes bipartisan bill to fund WisconsinEye
item.description: In a bipartisan about face, the Wisconsin Senate passed a bill Wednesday that includes nearly $600,000 in funding for WisconsinEye, the state's version of C-SPAN. The post Senate passes bipartisan bill to fund WisconsinEye appeared first on WPR.

item.title: Wisconsin Republicans announce plan to pass postpartum Medicaid, breast cancer bills
item.description: Republicans in the Wisconsin Assembly say they'll pass two bills related to women's health Thursday, a surprise move that comes after years of blocking the legislation. The post Wisconsin Republicans announce plan to pass postpartum Medicaid, breast cancer bills appeared first on WPR.
